prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name a single universally “best” roofer for every situation, but I can help you find the best one for your home. For hurricane-rated roof replacements in Miami you want a contractor who is experienced with the Florida Building Code (HVHZ), uses Miami‑Dade‑approved materials, and carries the right licensing, insurance and warranties.

How to find the best Miami roofer for hurricane-rated replacement
- Verify licensing and insurance
  - Check the contractor’s Florida roofing contractor license on the Florida DBPR license search.
  - Confirm they carry General Liability and Workers’ Compensation insurance and get certificates naming you as an additional insured while work is ongoing.
- Confirm product and installation approvals
  - Materials should be Miami‑Dade County approved (NOA) and rated for high wind/uplift. Ask to see the product NOA.
  - Installer should be familiar with Florida Building Code HVHZ requirements and able to show plans/inspection permits.
- Look for manufacturer certifications and warranties
  - Prefer contractors who are certified by major shingle/manufacturer programs (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred). Get both a workmanship warranty from the contractor and the manufacturer’s warranty for the product.
- Check track record and local experience
  - Ask for recent Miami-area hurricane-rated projects and references (ideally homes that endured storms).
  - Read Google, BBB, and local review sites. Check for any unresolved complaints or lawsuits.
- Get detailed written bids and scope
  - The bid should list materials (brand, model, wind rating), underlayment, fastener schedule, flashing details, deck attachment, ventilation, tear-off vs overlay, permit fees, cleanup and disposal, start/completion dates, and payment schedule (avoid large upfront payments).
- Permit, inspection and lien protection
  - Contractor should pull all permits and arrange inspections. Get conditional lien waivers with staged payments.
- Red flags
  - High-pressure sales tactics, cash-only requests, long delays to start with no reason, lack of written contract, no proof of insurance or license.

Questions to ask any contractor
- “Can you show your Florida contractor license and insurance certificates?”
- “Do the materials you propose have Miami‑Dade NOAs and are they rated for HVHZ?”
- “Do you have manufacturer certification with the product you’re installing?”
- “Who will pull permits and handle inspections?”
- “Can you provide three recent local references and photos of completed hurricane-rated roofs?”
- “What warranties do you offer (manufacturer and workmanship)?”

If you’d like, tell me your zip code or share 2–3 contractor names you’re considering and I’ll give guidance on how to compare them and what to look for in their estimates.
